Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).

Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.

Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high

ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-14847")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-14847")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host

| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.

Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound HTTPS to Mastra supply-chain C2 23.254.164.92:8000 and 23.254.164.123:443 · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Mastra dropper beacon file .pkg_history/.pkg_logs created by node in temp directory · [LLM] node.exe reading developer credential files shortly after npm install (Mastra stage-2) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process
easy-day-js postinstall hook running node setup.cjs --no-warnings AIInstallation High
Detects the @mastra supply-chain dropper's entry point: a node.exe process executing setup.cjs with the warning-suppression flag, almost always spawned from an npm/npx/yarn parent during package install. The string pair is unique to this campaign. Rationale: The literal cmdline pair 'setup.cjs' + '--no-warnings' is the postinstall hook defined in the malicious easy-day-js@1.11.22 package.json verbatim from the article. Combined with an npm/npx/yarn parent it has no legitimate analog in production environments. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/issues/18045 • https://app.stepsecurity.io/oss-security-feed/@mastra/schema-compat?version=1.2.12
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1546.016 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer-written test fixture literally named setup.cjs in an internal package's postinstall
  • Internal Node.js tooling that happens to chain --no-warnings into a build script called setup.cjs
  • Security research labs detonating the IOC sample for analysis
  • Vendored npm modules where a maintainer reused the filename setup.cjs for legitimate bootstrap
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("jest","mocha","vitest","--test") and ProcessCommandLine !contains "easy-day-js")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the host's npm/yarn lockfile and confirm if easy-day-js@1.11.22 or any @mastra package version listed in the article is resolved. Capture SHA256 of the setup.cjs file and compare against IOCs 221c45a7…, 4a886024…, ae70dd4f…. 2) Contain: isolate the host (developer workstation or CI runner), revoke any NPM_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/OPENAI_API_KEY/AWS keys present on the box, kill any node child process still running, force-rotate org-level npm publish tokens. 3) Hunt: pivot on InitiatingProcessAccountName + DeviceId to find any node child writing to %TEMP%\<24-hex>.js, any connection to 23.254.164.0/24, and any reads of ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.npmrc, or .github/workflows secrets directories in the 60 minutes following the postinstall.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "setup.cjs" and ProcessCommandLine has "--no-warnings"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","npm","npm-cli.js","npx.exe","npx","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","cmd.exe","bash","sh")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\node.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "/node"
| where CommandLine has "setup.cjs" and CommandLine has "--no-warnings"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("npm.exe","npm-cli.js","npx.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","cmd.exe","bash","sh")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Outbound HTTPS to Mastra supply-chain C2 23.254.164.92:8000 and 23.254.164.123:443 AICommand & Control Medium
Alerts on any host (dev workstation or CI runner) connecting to the stage-1 download server 23.254.164.92:8000 or stage-2 exfil server 23.254.164.123:443, including their hostwinds DNS aliases. These IPs and the /update/<numeric-id> URI shape are unique to this campaign. Rationale: Both /24-adjacent IPs and both hostwinds aliases are explicit IOCs in the article body and kill-chain reconstruction. The /update/49890878 URI path is the literal stage-1 endpoint copied verbatim from the article. Any hit is a high-fidelity infection indicator. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/issues/18045 • https://app.stepsecurity.io/oss-security-feed/@mastra/schema-compat?version=1.2.12
ATT&CKT1105 T1071.001 T1571 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat intelligence analysts manually visiting the C2 from a sandbox
  • Internal blue-team red-team exercises replaying the IOC list
  • Internet-wide scanners (Censys, Shodan, Project Discovery) operating from corporate egress
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("WindowsSandboxClient.exe","sandbox.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the InitiatingProcessFileName for the connection — if it's node.exe with a parent of npm/npx/yarn, treat as confirmed Mastra supply-chain infection. Capture the full lockfile and resolved easy-day-js / @mastra package versions. 2) Contain: block 23.254.164.0/24 and both hwsrv-1327785/6.hostwindsdns.com at perimeter and proxy, isolate any host that connected, kill all node child processes. 3) Hunt: rotate every secret accessible from that host: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, AWS keys, GITHUB_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN. Search SigninLogs / CloudTrail / GitHub audit log for any use of those tokens from non-corporate IPs in the 24h window starting at the first connection.
let badIPs = dynamic(["23.254.164.92","23.254.164.123"]);
let badDomains = dynamic(["hwsrv-1327786.hostwindsdns.com","hwsrv-1327785.hostwindsdns.com"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (badIPs)
   or RemoteUrl has_any (badDomains)
   or RemoteUrl has "/update/49890878"
| extend Stage = case(RemoteIP == "23.254.164.92" or RemoteUrl has "hwsrv-1327786", "Stage1-Download",
                     RemoteIP == "23.254.164.123" or RemoteUrl has "hwsrv-1327785", "Stage2-Exfil", "Unknown")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, Stage, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
let badIPs = dynamic(["23.254.164.92","23.254.164.123"]);
let badDomains = dynamic(["hwsrv-1327786.hostwindsdns.com","hwsrv-1327785.hostwindsdns.com"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DestinationIP in (badIPs) or DestinationHostName in (badDomains) or RequestURL has "/update/49890878"
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, DeviceVendor),
(DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Name in (badDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, IPAddresses=RemoteIp),
(ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DstIpAddr in (badIPs) or DstHostname in (badDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, DstHostname, Url)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Mastra Supply-Chain C2 Network Connection (23.254.164.92 / 23.254.164.123)
id: 9c8f1d2e-4b3a-44e1-9d52-c6f9c7e2a83a
description: Detects outbound connection to the @mastra npm supply-chain attack C2 infrastructure used by easy-day-js@1.11.22 dropper
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/144-mastra-npm-packages-compromised-via.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/17
tags:

logsource:

  product: windows
detection:
  selection_ip:
    DestinationIp:
      - '23.254.164.92'
      - '23.254.164.123'
  selection_dns:
    DestinationHostname:
      - 'hwsrv-1327786.hostwindsdns.com'
      - 'hwsrv-1327785.hostwindsdns.com'
  condition: selection_ip or selection_dns
level: critical
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 (@DestinationIp:(23.254.164.92 OR 23.254.164.123) OR @DestinationHostname:(hwsrv-1327786.hostwindsdns.com OR hwsrv-1327785.hostwindsdns.com))) OR (source:windows.defender @RemoteUrl:(*hwsrv-1327786* OR *hwsrv-1327785* OR */update/49890878*))
(#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 (RemoteAddressIP4="23.254.164.92" OR RemoteAddressIP4="23.254.164.123")) OR (#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/hwsrv-132778[56]\.hostwindsdns\.com/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort, DomainName], function=count())
NETWORK

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.app) as app sum(All_Traffic.bytes_out) as bytes_out sum(All_Traffic.bytes_in) as bytes_in from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest_ip IN ("23.254.164.92","23.254.164.123")) (All_Traffic.dest_port IN (8000,443)) by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.dest_ip All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.app) as app sum(All_Traffic.bytes_out) as bytes_out sum(All_Traffic.bytes_in) as bytes_in from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest_ip IN ("23.254.164.92","23.254.164.123")) (All_Traffic.dest_port IN (8000,443)) by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.dest_ip All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Node spawning detached script from %TEMP% with 24-hex filename and host:port argv (stage-2) AIInstallation High
Hunts the stage-2 execution shape unique to this dropper: node.exe launching a script whose basename matches ^[a-f0-9]{24}\.js$ located in the OS temp directory, with the stage-2 C2 host:port (e.g. 23.254.164.123:443) passed as the second argv. This combination is artifact-driven and has no legitimate analog. Rationale: The 24-hex-char .js filename in tmpdir and host:port argv pattern come directly from the kill-chain reconstruction's quoted spawn signature: child_process.spawn(process.execPath, [filepath, stage2C2], {cwd: os.tmpdir(), detached: true}). Both the filename shape and the trailing host:port argv are highly specific.
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1105 T1564.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • npm pack/install creating randomly-named cache files that happen to match the 24-hex pattern (rare — npm uses longer hashes)
  • Internal build tools generating obfuscated cache files in TEMP
  • Electron app updaters writing temp staging scripts (typically named app-update.js etc., not bare hex)
Response runbook
1) Triage: extract the Stage2Target column — if it resolves to 23.254.164.0/24 or hwsrv-1327785.hostwindsdns.com, treat as confirmed Mastra C2 callback. Capture the .js file from %TEMP% before it self-deletes. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the detached node process tree, preserve %TEMP% contents for forensics, block stage-2 IP/domain at perimeter. 3) Hunt: enumerate every secret on the host (env vars, ~/.aws, ~/.npmrc, ~/.config/gh, GitHub Actions runner secrets), assume compromised, rotate. Pivot on the package.json that pulled in easy-day-js to identify other infected hosts.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(?:\\Temp\\|AppData\\Local\\Temp\\|/tmp/)[a-f0-9]{24}\.js\s+\S+:\d{2,5}"
| extend Stage2Target = extract(@"([a-zA-Z0-9\.\-]+:\d{2,5})\s*$", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, Stage2Target, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\node.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "/node"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(?:\\Temp\\|AppData\\Local\\Temp\\|/tmp/)[a-f0-9]{24}\.js\s+\S+:\d{2,5}"
| extend Stage2Target = extract(@"([a-zA-Z0-9\.\-]+:\d{2,5})\s*$", 1, CommandLine)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, Stage2Target, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE) @CommandLine:(*\\Temp\\* OR *AppData\\Local\\Temp* OR */tmp/*) @CommandLine:(*23.254.164.123* OR *.js\ *:443* OR *.js\ *:8000*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\node\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)(\\\\Temp\\\\|AppData\\\\Local\\\\Temp\\\\|/tmp/)[a-f0-9]{24}\\.js\\s+\\S+:\\d{2,5}", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent values(Processes.process_hash) as hash from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name=node.exe OR Processes.process_name=node) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | regex process="(?i)(?:[\\\/]Temp[\\\/]|AppData[\\\/]Local[\\\/]Temp[\\\/]|\/tmp\/)[a-f0-9]{24}\.js\s+\S+:\d{2,5}" | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent values(Processes.process_hash) as hash from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name=node.exe OR Processes.process_name=node) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | regex process="(?i)(?:[\\\/]Temp[\\\/]|AppData[\\\/]Local[\\\/]Temp[\\\/]|\/tmp\/)[a-f0-9]{24}\.js\s+\S+:\d{2,5}" | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
npm install referencing compromised @mastra packages or easy-day-js dependency AIDelivery High
Hunts hosts and CI runners executing npm/yarn/pnpm install that explicitly name easy-day-js or one of the 13 compromised @mastra package versions. Catches both intentional installs and those triggered by lockfile updates that resolved during the 36-minute attack window on 2026-06-17. Rationale: The full list of 13 compromised @mastra packages plus the easy-day-js typosquat dependency name come directly from the article's affected-versions table. Any command-line reference is article-specific by definition — this name was registered as a typosquat purely for this campaign. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/issues/18045
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1199
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security-aware developers running `npm view easy-day-js` to inspect the IOC
  • Incident-response forensic captures of infected lockfiles being read on analyst workstations
  • Mastra framework users who legitimately depend on @mastra/core but pinned to versions BEFORE 1.42.1 (the malicious release)
  • SCA tooling like socket.dev or snyk scanning package metadata
Suppression filter
| where ProcessCommandLine !has_any ("npm view","npm info","npm search","socket.dev","snyk","--dry-run")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the host's package-lock.json/yarn.lock actually RESOLVED easy-day-js@1.11.22 (cmdline can name a package without installing the malicious version if pinned). Check resolved version, not declared range. 2) Contain: if the malicious version is resolved, isolate, rotate every secret accessible from that host (LLM keys, AWS, GitHub, NPM), purge node_modules and lockfile, force-pin @mastra packages to known-good versions. 3) Hunt: query CI/CD systems for any pipeline run between 2026-06-17 01:01 UTC and present that did `npm install` for any of the 13 affected packages — those builds installed the malicious dependency and any secrets in the runner environment must be considered burned.
let compromised = dynamic(["easy-day-js","@mastra/schema-compat","@mastra/core","@mastra/memory","@mastra/server","@mastra/deployer","@mastra/pg","@mastra/mcp","@mastra/libsql","@mastra/evals","@mastra/datadog","@mastra/rag","@mastra/deployer-vercel","@mastra/redis"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("npm.exe","npm","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","node.exe") or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","npm","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (compromised) or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (compromised)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
let compromised = dynamic(["easy-day-js","@mastra/schema-compat","@mastra/core","@mastra/memory","@mastra/server","@mastra/deployer","@mastra/pg","@mastra/mcp","@mastra/libsql","@mastra/evals","@mastra/datadog","@mastra/rag","@mastra/deployer-vercel","@mastra/redis"]);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has_any ("npm.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","node.exe")
| where CommandLine has_any (compromised)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Mastra dropper beacon file .pkg_history/.pkg_logs created by node in temp directory AIActions on Objectives High
Detects creation of the campaign's victim-fingerprint files (.pkg_history, .pkg_logs) written to the OS temp directory by a node.exe process. These filenames are unique to the easy-day-js dropper and are used to record install path and compromised package name. Rationale: The .pkg_history and .pkg_logs file names in temp are explicit IOCs from the kill-chain reconstruction's quoted detection hint: 'Beacon: record install path and package name in tmp dir'. These dotfile names with that path constraint and node.exe writer have no benign analog.
ATT&CKT1083 T1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Custom internal npm tooling that happens to write a similarly-named beacon file
  • Other npm packages legitimately using .pkg_history (none known)
  • Forensic capture replay during IR exercises
Response runbook
1) Triage: read the contents of the .pkg_history / .pkg_logs file to confirm it lists @mastra package paths and easy-day-js. Capture the file before the dropper self-cleans. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill any node child, block 23.254.164.0/24 at egress, preserve %TEMP% for forensics. 3) Hunt: pivot on InitiatingProcessAccountName + DeviceId — query the previous 30 days of DeviceProcessEvents for the postinstall hook (UC1) and DeviceNetworkEvents for the C2 IPs (UC2) to scope the dwell time. Treat any secret accessible from this host as burned and rotate.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType == "FileCreated"
| where FileName in~ (".pkg_history",".pkg_logs")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Temp\", "/tmp/", @"AppData\Local\Temp")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated"
| where TargetFileName in~ (".pkg_history",".pkg_logs")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Temp\", "/tmp/", @"AppData\Local\Temp")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","node")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Mastra Dropper Beacon File .pkg_history/.pkg_logs in Temp
id: 4a2b8c1d-9e3f-4b5a-87d2-1f6a3c4e9b21
description: Detects the easy-day-js dropper writing its victim-fingerprint files (.pkg_history / .pkg_logs) into the OS temp directory
references:

author: SOC Detection Engineering

logsource:

level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\\Temp\\.pkg_history OR *\\Temp\\.pkg_logs OR *AppData\\Local\\Temp\\.pkg_history OR *AppData\\Local\\Temp\\.pkg_logs OR */tmp/.pkg_history OR */tmp/.pkg_logs) @Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten ContextImageFileName=/\\node\.exe$/i TargetFileName=/(\\Temp\\|AppData\\Local\\Temp\\|\/tmp\/)\.(pkg_history|pkg_logs)$/i

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.process_name) as proc values(Filesystem.file_path) as path from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name IN (".pkg_history",".pkg_logs")) Filesystem.action=created by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | search path="*\\Temp\\*" OR path="*/tmp/*" OR path="*AppData\\Local\\Temp*" | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)

node.exe reading developer credential files shortly after npm install (Mastra stage-2) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the stage-2 credential harvest behaviour: a node.exe process reading ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml, or the GitHub Actions runner secrets directory shortly after an npm install. Aligns with the article's assessment that the dropper steals LLM/cloud/VCS tokens for exfil to 23.254.164.123:443. Rationale: Credential file paths (~/.aws/credentials, ~/.config/gh, GitHub Actions runner _temp dir, .npmrc) are from the kill-chain reconstruction's phase 8 quoted hint. The 10-minute join after npm install scopes to the dropper's actual execution window, cutting false positives from cloud-CLI tooling that legitimately reads these files at other times.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.005 T1083
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • aws-cli wrappers shelling out to node and immediately reading ~/.aws/credentials
  • Vercel/Netlify deploy CLI authenticated via gh token reading hosts.yml during build
  • Internal CI bootstrappers that read .npmrc as a normal part of npm install (would need refinement to filter)
  • Electron-based dev tools indexing user dotfiles for autocomplete
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("aws-sdk","@aws-sdk","vercel","netlify","firebase-tools")
Response runbook
1) Triage: cross-reference DeviceName + AccountName against UC4 hits (compromised @mastra install) and UC2 hits (C2 callback). Three-way correlation = high-confidence credential theft. 2) Contain: force-rotate every cred read by node — AWS keys in ~/.aws, GitHub PAT in ~/.config/gh, NPM publish tokens in ~/.npmrc, SSH keys. For CI runners, revoke runner registration tokens and re-provision. 3) Hunt: pivot the stolen credentials to CloudTrail/AzureActivity/GitHub audit log — search for the rotated AWS access key's last-used location, any unfamiliar IPs on the GitHub token usage, and any new npm publish events under the developer's account in the 24h post-infection window.
let CredentialReads = DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where (FolderPath has @"\.aws\" and FileName == "credentials")
    or (FolderPath has "/.aws/" and FileName == "credentials")
    or (FolderPath has @"\.config\gh\" and FileName == "hosts.yml")
    or (FolderPath has "/.config/gh/" and FileName == "hosts.yml")
    or (FolderPath has @"\.ssh\" and FileName matches regex @"^id_(rsa|ed25519|ecdsa)$")
    or (FolderPath has "Runner.Worker" and FolderPath has "_temp")
    or FileName =~ ".npmrc";
let RecentNpmInstall = DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "npm" and ProcessCommandLine has "install"
| project NpmTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, NpmUser = AccountName;
CredentialReads
| join kind=inner RecentNpmInstall on DeviceId
| where Timestamp between (NpmTime .. NpmTime + 10m)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, NpmTime, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, NpmTime), InitiatingProcessAccountName, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let CredReads = ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","node")
| where (TargetFilePath has @"\.aws\" and TargetFileName == "credentials")
    or (TargetFilePath has "/.aws/" and TargetFileName == "credentials")
    or (TargetFilePath has @"\.config\gh\" and TargetFileName == "hosts.yml")
    or (TargetFilePath has "/.config/gh/" and TargetFileName == "hosts.yml")
    or TargetFileName =~ ".npmrc"
    or (TargetFilePath has "Runner.Worker" and TargetFilePath has "_temp");
let NpmRuns = ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "npm" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "install"
| project NpmTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, NpmUser = ActorUsername;
CredReads
| join kind=inner NpmRuns on DvcHostname
| where TimeGenerated between (NpmTime .. NpmTime + 10m)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, NpmTime, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', TimeGenerated, NpmTime), ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE) @TargetFilename:(*\\.aws\\credentials OR */.aws/credentials OR *\\.config\\gh\\hosts.yml OR */.config/gh/hosts.yml OR *\\.ssh\\id_rsa OR */.ssh/id_rsa OR *Runner.Worker*_temp*)
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo ContextImageFileName=/\\node\.exe$/i
| regex("(\\\\\\.aws\\\\credentials|/\\.aws/credentials|\\\\\\.config\\\\gh\\\\hosts\\.yml|/\\.config/gh/hosts\\.yml|\\\\\\.ssh\\\\id_(rsa|ed25519|ecdsa)|Runner\\.Worker.*_temp)", field=TargetFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths values(Filesystem.process_name) as proc from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name=node.exe (Filesystem.file_path="*\\.aws\\credentials*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.config\\gh\\hosts.yml*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gh/hosts.yml*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.ssh\\id_rsa*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_rsa*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*Runner.Worker*secret*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*_temp\\_runner_file_commands*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths values(Filesystem.process_name) as proc from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name=node.exe (Filesystem.file_path="*\\.aws\\credentials*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.config\\gh\\hosts.yml*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gh/hosts.yml*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.ssh\\id_rsa*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_rsa*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*Runner.Worker*secret*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*_temp\\_runner_file_commands*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High

DeviceNetworkEvents

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Joomla JCE editor profile creation and PHP upload via unauthenticated endpoint (CVE-2026-48907) AIExploitation High
Hunts the article's specific JCE Editor exploit chain: unauthenticated POSTs to the JCE plugin endpoints (com_jce / jce / imgmanager) that create editor profiles and then upload .php / .phtml / .phar files. Targets web-tier telemetry where the exploit is observable. Rationale: Anchors directly on the JCE endpoints (com_jce / imgmanager / editor profile) named by CISA + Widget Factory's advisory, paired with PHP upload extensions. Cross-checked against the CISA KEV entry and Widget Factory 2.9.99.5 release notes. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog • https://www.joomlacontenteditor.net/
ATT&CKT1190 T1505.003
Data sourcesWeb.Web Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Joomla site admin updating JCE editor profiles from the back end
  • Webmaster uploading vetted PHP through the JCE file browser
  • Joomla penetration test exercising com_jce
  • Migration/backup tools writing PHP files into media/jce/
  • Authenticated content editor with profile-edit rights
Suppression filter
| where not (cIP in ("<admin-jumpbox-ip>")) and not (csUserAgent has "Joomla-Manage")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Confirm the source IP is not on the admin allowlist, pull the full request body / referer, and check whether the JCE component version is < 2.9.99.5 on the targeted host. Step 2 — Contain: Block the source IP at the WAF, quarantine and hash any PHP file dropped under /images, /components/com_jce, or /media/jce, and force a Joomla session reset. Step 3 — Hunt: Pivot on the offending source IP for other unauthenticated POSTs to com_jce across the estate, search wp/Joomla file systems for additional PHP shells matching the same SHA256, and review web server child processes spawned from w3wp/httpd/php-fpm in the last 7 days.

PHP webshell file actions originating from web server process (Beloved PBN wp_posts shell) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the Sucuri-described PHP web shell embedded in wp_posts that exposes read/write/edit/delete/chmod/upload over HTTP. Targets the web-server process (w3wp / php-fpm / httpd) performing untrusted file operations across the document root immediately after a POST hits /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php or /index.php. Rationale: Mirrors Sucuri's description of the wp_posts-resident shell that performs read/write/edit/delete/chmod/rename/upload over HTTP — only the web-server process should be writing PHP outside of plugin upgrade paths. Cross-referenced with the article's Sucuri callout. Cross-checked against: • https://blog.sucuri.net/
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate WordPress / Joomla plugin install or auto-update
  • Composer or wp-cli running PHP file deployments
  • Site-migration / staging-sync tooling (e.g. WP Migrate, Duplicator)
  • Cache plugins writing object-cache.php to wp-content/
  • Manual hotfix uploaded via SFTP that triggers web-server rewrite of .htaccess
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("wp-cli.phar","composer.phar","composer")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Pull every PHP/.htaccess write by the web-server process in the cluster, hash them and check whether they originate from an authentic plugin update by cross-checking against wp-admin/admin-ajax.php request logs. Step 2 — Contain: Take the host offline behind maintenance mode, snapshot disk + database (focus on wp_posts content where post_content begins with `<?php`), and rotate all wp-config secrets + DB creds. Step 3 — Hunt: Query for inbound HTTP requests with body parameters matching shell commands (read/write/edit/delete/chmod) over the last 30 days, search every site in the estate for wp_posts rows where post_content contains `<?php`, and review egress traffic from the web tier for the IOCs in UC4.

WordPress backdoor admin account created via injected JavaScript (OptinMonster/TrustPulse supply chain) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the Sansec-described supply chain campaign where injected JS waits for a logged-in admin and silently submits POSTs to /wp-admin/user-new.php and /wp-admin/plugin-install.php to create a backdoor admin and install a self-hiding plugin. Pivots on unattended user/plugin creation calls coming from a logged-in admin session shortly after page load. Rationale: Anchored on the article's named WP admin endpoints (user-new.php / plugin-install.php) which the Sansec write-up identified as the actions the injected JS silently triggers in an admin session. Cross-checked against: • https://sansec.io/research/
ATT&CKT1136.001 T1505 T1195.002
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate site administrator manually creating a new editor / installing a plugin
  • Bulk WordPress provisioning via WP-CLI or a managed-hosting control panel
  • Pen-test exercise creating admin via the UI
  • Cookie-based plugin installer (e.g. ManageWP, Jetpack) actioning a fleet install
  • Authenticated admin walking through site-setup wizard
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Identify the WordPress site, confirm whether the source IP and User-Agent correspond to a known admin, and pull the list of users + plugins created in the last 7 days. Step 2 — Contain: Disable any user created in the suspicious window, remove unknown plugins, force password reset for all admins, rotate ABSPATH secrets/salts, and revoke active sessions. Step 3 — Hunt: Search the site's HTML for outbound JS includes pointing at OptinMonster/TrustPulse/PushEngage CDN paths that were compromised, audit wp_options for hidden-plugin flags (e.g. `active_plugins` containing entries that don't appear in wp-admin), and pivot on the source IP across all monitored sites.

Hunts outbound network connections or DNS queries to the article's named IOCs (tidio.cc, 84.201.6.54) — which the Beloved PBN Entegrasyonu fake plugin beacons to on every page load. Tier as alerting because both indicators are specific, low-volume, and second-source confirmed. Rationale: Both IOCs are named explicitly in the article (tidio.cc, 84.201.6.54). Specific enough to alert on outright; cross-checked against abuse.ch ThreatFox and the Sucuri write-up referenced in the article. Cross-checked against: • https://threatfox.abuse.ch/ • https://blog.sucuri.net/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate site using Tidio.com live-chat that mis-resolves to the typo-squat tidio.cc (rare but worth checking)
  • Threat-intel feed ingest tooling fetching the IOC for analysis
  • Security researcher pivot from a sandbox host
  • Mis-routed traffic on a shared NAT egress IP belonging to a hosting provider that legitimately uses 84.201.6.0/24
  • Scheduled IOC enrichment job pulling the domain into a TI platform
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("misp.exe","opencti.exe","powershell.exe") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "ThreatIntel"
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Confirm whether the source is a production web tier, identify the initiating process and parent, and check whether the site hosts WordPress or Joomla with the JCE plugin installed. Step 2 — Contain: Block 84.201.6.54 and *.tidio.cc at the perimeter (egress + DNS sinkhole), and isolate the affected web host pending PHP webshell hunt (see UC2). Step 3 — Hunt: Pivot on every host that resolved tidio.cc in the last 90 days, inspect wp_options / wp_posts for the Beloved PBN Entegrasyonu plugin signature, and search outbound page HTML for PBN backlinks injected into the footer.
let IocIPs = dynamic(["84.201.6.54"]);
let IocDomains = dynamic(["tidio.cc"]);
union
(DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (IocIPs) or RemoteUrl has_any (IocDomains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Protocol),
(DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse"
| where RemoteUrl has_any (IocDomains) or AdditionalFields has_any (IocDomains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, AdditionalFields)
| order by Timestamp desc
let IocIPs = dynamic(["84.201.6.54"]);
let IocDomains = dynamic(["tidio.cc"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DestinationIP in (IocIPs) or DestinationHostName has_any (IocDomains) or RequestURL has_any (IocDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, DeviceAction),
(DnsEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Name has_any (IocDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, ResultCode),
(ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DnsQuery has_any (IocDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName, EventResult),
(ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr in (IocIPs) or DstHostname has_any (IocDomains) or Url has_any (IocDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol),
(W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where csReferer has_any (IocDomains) or csHost has_any (IocDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csUriStem, csHost, csReferer)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Beacon to JCE/Beloved-PBN Campaign IOCs (tidio.cc / 84.201.6.54)
id: 7c9d8e2f-1a44-4a3b-9f51-aab7e2bcb0d2
description: Detects outbound network traffic or DNS resolution to the IOCs Sucuri/CISA associated with the Joomla JCE exploitation and Beloved PBN Entegrasyonu fake plugin campaign.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/cisa-warns-of-actively-exploited-joomla.html
author: detection-engineering
date: 2026/06/17
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1568
logsource:
  category: dns
detection:
  selection:
    query|endswith:
      - 'tidio.cc'
  condition: selection
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:(3 OR 22) (@DestinationIp:84.201.6.54 OR @DestinationHostname:*tidio.cc OR @QueryName:*tidio.cc)) OR (source:(linux.auditd OR linux.syslog OR nginx OR apache OR iis) (@network.destination.ip:84.201.6.54 OR @dns.question.name:*tidio.cc OR @http.url:*tidio.cc*))
(#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 RemoteAddressIP4="84.201.6.54")
OR (#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(^|\.)tidio\.cc$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4, DomainName], function=count())
# log group: /aws/vpc/flowlogs
fields @timestamp, srcAddr, dstAddr, dstPort, action, bytes
| filter dstAddr = "84.201.6.54"
| stats count() as conns, sum(bytes) as bytes by srcAddr, dstAddr, dstPort
| sort conns desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.dest_ip) as dest_ip values(All_Traffic.dest) as dest values(All_Traffic.src) as src values(All_Traffic.process) as process values(All_Traffic.user) as user from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest_ip="84.201.6.54" OR All_Traffic.dest="*tidio.cc*") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest_ip All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| appendpipe [| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(DNS.src) as src values(DNS.query) as query from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where DNS.query="*tidio.cc" by DNS.src DNS.query | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.dest_ip) as dest_ip values(All_Traffic.dest) as dest values(All_Traffic.src) as src values(All_Traffic.process) as process values(All_Traffic.user) as user from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest_ip="84.201.6.54" OR All_Traffic.dest="*tidio.cc*") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest_ip All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| appendpipe [| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(DNS.src) as src values(DNS.query) as query from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where DNS.query="*tidio.cc" by DNS.src DNS.query | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents

let BadIPs     = dynamic(["84.201.6.54"]);

   or Url has_any (BadDomains)

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent

                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",

| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48907")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48907")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-48907")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-48907")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Actions on Objectives
—
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Vulnerable rclone --rc-serve deployment without HTTP authentication · [LLM] Rclone RC listener bound to non-loopback interface via --rc-addr · [LLM] Devices with vulnerable rclone (CVE-2026-49980) in software inventory · Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Browser process initiating connection to local rclone RC port 5572
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Rclone process spawns command interpreter (CVE-2026-49980 post-exploit)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Rclone process spawns command interpreter (CVE-2026-49980 post-exploit) AIExploitation High
Detects rclone spawning a shell or scripting interpreter, which is the observable behaviour when CVE-2026-49980 inline-remote backend options execute commands as the rclone process user. Rclone is a pure Go binary and does not normally shell out, so a process-tree pivot from rclone to bash/cmd/powershell/python is very high-fidelity evidence the unauthenticated RCE has fired. Rationale: Article confirms 'execute commands as the rclone process user' via inline backend option overrides. Rclone is a single-binary Go program with no legitimate need to fork shells/interpreters in production, so parent=rclone + child=shell is the cleanest post-exploit telemetry. Cross-checked against CCB Belgium advisory and rclone changelog confirming CVE-2026-49980 fixed in 1.74.3. Cross-checked against: • https://ccb.belgium.be/advisories/warning-two-critical-unauthenticated-code-execution-vulnerabilities-rclone-patch • https://securityonline.info/rclone-command-execution/ • https://rclone.org/changelog/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059 T1203
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Backup/DevOps wrapper scripts that invoke rclone from a shell and the shell parent is mis-attributed by Sysmon when rapid re-parenting happens
  • Rclone container images using shell-based ENTRYPOINT/CMD wrappers (entrypoint.sh) that re-exec rclone — child may appear inverted
  • Custom rclone backends using --script-pre-list or operator wrappers that legitimately fork helper interpreters
  • Admin live-troubleshooting rclone interactively from a shell pipe (rclone | jq, rclone | grep)
  • Container init systems (tini, dumb-init) that briefly mediate the rclone process tree
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/entrypoint.sh", "tini --", "dumb-init")) and not (ChildCmd has_any (" | jq", " | grep", " | awk", " | tee"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full child ProcessCommandLine and parent rclone command line; confirm parent rclone had --rc-serve and no --rc-user/--rc-pass/--rc-htpasswd flag. Check rclone version on host — vulnerable range is 1.55.0 to 1.74.2. 2) Contain: kill the rclone PID and any descendant processes; block inbound to the RC port (default 5572) at host firewall; if internet-facing, take the host off the network. Preserve memory if forensics is needed before kill. 3) Hunt: pivot on the host for any DeviceProcessEvents with rclone as ancestor in last 30 days, web-server / proxy logs for inbound GET/HEAD to port 5572, and outbound connections from the spawned shell (egress = data exfil or second-stage download). Check DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities for other hosts with the same CVE.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("rclone.exe", "rclone")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("rcd", "--rc-serve", "--rc ", "--rc-addr")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","bash","sh","dash","zsh","ksh","python","python3","perl","ruby","node")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentFolderPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildFolderPath = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend ParentLeaf = tolower(tostring(split(ParentProcessName, "\\")[-1])),
         ChildLeaf  = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| where ParentLeaf in ("rclone.exe", "rclone")
| where ChildLeaf in ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","bash","sh","dash","zsh","ksh","python","python3","perl","ruby","node")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Vulnerable rclone --rc-serve deployment without HTTP authentication AIReconnaissance High
Hunts for rclone processes started with the --rc-serve flag but without --rc-user, --rc-pass, or --rc-htpasswd — the exact precondition the advisory calls out as enabling unauthenticated CVE-2026-49980 RCE. Surfaces vulnerable surfaces before they are exploited. Rationale: Article explicitly states the preconditions: '--rc-serve flag must be in use' AND 'deployed without global RC HTTP authentication - so not using --rc-user/--rc-pass/--rc-htpasswd'. Detecting this combination on the command line directly enumerates the vulnerable population before an attacker reaches them. Validated against rclone docs and CCB Belgium advisory. Cross-checked against: • https://ccb.belgium.be/advisories/warning-two-critical-unauthenticated-code-execution-vulnerabilities-rclone-patch • https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_rcd/
ATT&CKT1190 T1133
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal-only lab rclone instances where auth is intentionally skipped because the host is air-gapped — still a misconfig but not exploitable
  • Rclone WebGUI demos / training environments
  • Rclone running with auth provided via env var or config file rather than CLI flag (real auth, false positive on this rule)
  • rclone rcd test runs by admins during config validation
  • Docker containers where rclone reads --rc-user from a mounted secret file using `--rc-user-from-file` style indirection
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the rclone version on the host (vulnerable range 1.55.0–1.74.2); check whether the host is reachable from untrusted networks (`netstat -ano | findstr 5572` or `ss -ltnp | grep 5572` and correlate to allowed-ingress firewall rules). 2) Contain: if internet-facing, add inbound block for TCP 5572 immediately; otherwise notify owner with 24h SLA to either upgrade to 1.74.3+, add --rc-user/--rc-pass, or stop using --rc-serve. 3) Hunt: pivot to last 30 days of inbound connections to port 5572 on that host and any rclone child-process shell-spawn events (UC1) to determine if exploitation has already occurred.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("rclone.exe", "rclone")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "--rc-serve"
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--rc-user", "--rc-pass", "--rc-htpasswd"))
| extend RcAddr = extract(@"--rc-addr[\s=]+(\S+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, RcAddr, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend Leaf = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| where Leaf in ("rclone.exe", "rclone")
| where CommandLine has "--rc-serve"
| where not (CommandLine has_any ("--rc-user", "--rc-pass", "--rc-htpasswd"))
| extend RcAddr = extract(@"--rc-addr[\s=]+(\S+)", 1, CommandLine)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, RcAddr
| order by TimeGenerated desc
