Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url

    [| tstats `summariesonly` count

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",

Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents

// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:

let LookbackDays = 7d;

    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("3715092aa00f380cefe8b4d2eddb7d08", "7cef19f9c4480adac0cd4702ff98f46c", "7eb9cee1f696727752169f25cf79a338", "b6b0602310bb2d4360c52685119aac1b") or SHA1 in~ ("3715092aa00f380cefe8b4d2eddb7d08", "7cef19f9c4480adac0cd4702ff98f46c", "7eb9cee1f696727752169f25cf79a338", "b6b0602310bb2d4360c52685119aac1b") or MD5 in~ ("3715092aa00f380cefe8b4d2eddb7d08", "7cef19f9c4480adac0cd4702ff98f46c", "7eb9cee1f696727752169f25cf79a338", "b6b0602310bb2d4360c52685119aac1b")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("3715092aa00f380cefe8b4d2eddb7d08", "7cef19f9c4480adac0cd4702ff98f46c", "7eb9cee1f696727752169f25cf79a338", "b6b0602310bb2d4360c52685119aac1b") or SHA1 in~ ("3715092aa00f380cefe8b4d2eddb7d08", "7cef19f9c4480adac0cd4702ff98f46c", "7eb9cee1f696727752169f25cf79a338", "b6b0602310bb2d4360c52685119aac1b") or MD5 in~ ("3715092aa00f380cefe8b4d2eddb7d08", "7cef19f9c4480adac0cd4702ff98f46c", "7eb9cee1f696727752169f25cf79a338", "b6b0602310bb2d4360c52685119aac1b")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["3715092aa00f380cefe8b4d2eddb7d08", "7cef19f9c4480adac0cd4702ff98f46c", "7eb9cee1f696727752169f25cf79a338", "b6b0602310bb2d4360c52685119aac1b"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Cisco Releases Security Updates for Actively Exploited SD-WAN Manager Flaw

The Hacker News
2026-06-16 7 use cases 2 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Cisco has released security updates for a medium-severity security flaw in Catalyst SD-WAN Manager that has come under active exploitation in the wild. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-20262, carries a CVSS score of 6.5 out of 10.0. "A vulnerability in the web UI of Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, formerly SD-WAN vManage, could allow an authenticated, remote attacker to create a file or

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] vManage SdraAnyConnect handler writes WAR via path traversal
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Wildfly WFLYSRV0010 deploys non-baseline WAR on vManage · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Cisco Releases Security Updates for Actively Exploited SD-WAN Manager Flaw
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] vManage service-proxy POST to attacker-deployed JSP webshell · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
vManage SdraAnyConnect handler writes WAR via path traversal AIExploitation High
Hunts for the CVE-2026-20262 exploitation signal in vmanage-server.log — the AnyConnect file-upload handler logging an 'uploaded Remote Access Anyconnect profile file' record whose destination path contains '../' or lands a .war/.jsp in the Wildfly deployments folder. Legitimate AnyConnect profile uploads never traverse path, so this is the high-fidelity arbitrary-file-write primitive. Rationale: Anchored on the exact log line from the Cisco advisory body: 'SdraAnyConnectFileUploadHandler ... uploaded Remote Access Anyconnect profile file: ../../../../var/lib/wildfly/standalone/deployments/suspicious.war'. The combination of the handler name + literal action string + a traversal sequence in the destination is uniquely associated with CVE-2026-20262 exploitation. Cross-checked against the Cisco PSIRT advisory and BleepingComputer write-up. Cross-checked against: • https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-sdwan-arbfw-c2rZvQ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/cisco-fixes-sd-wan-vmanage-flaw-exploited-in-zero-day-attacks/ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/cisco-sd-wan-vmanage-vulnerability-exploit/
ATT&CKT1190 T1505.003
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Cisco TAC-guided diagnostic upload that intentionally crafts a path traversal for debugging (rare, planned)
  • Internal red-team or PSIRT-led pen test against the vManage cluster
  • Legacy AnyConnect XML profile naming that includes a '..' literal in the filename but not as a traversal (unlikely — vManage strips these)
  • Backup/restore tooling staging WAR/JSP files via the AnyConnect API endpoint (non-standard, vendor-supported tooling uses different endpoints)
Suppression filter
and not (UploadedPath matches regex @"^/var/lib/cisco/profiles/[a-z0-9_-]+\.xml$")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full vmanage-server.log record + 5-min window around it. Capture the session id from the bracket prefix (e.g. a66cdc5f-807d-4c23-944e-5c809a2ece6b), the authenticated username, source IP from the vManage audit log. 2) Contain: snapshot the appliance, remove the dropped artefact from /var/lib/wildfly/standalone/deployments/, disable the suspected admin account, isolate the vManage from edge routers if cluster-managed. 3) Hunt: pivot on the same session id and source IP in vmanage-appserver.log for WFLYSRV0010 deployments and in serviceproxy-access.log for POSTs to the deployed JSP path; check for lateral pivots to controller/validator nodes; review NMS audit log for policy changes by the same user.
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where SyslogMessage has "SdraAnyConnectFileUploadHandler"
| where SyslogMessage has "uploaded Remote Access Anyconnect profile file"
| extend UploadedPath = extract(@"file:\s+(\S+)\s+to\s+vManage", 1, SyslogMessage)
| where UploadedPath has "../" or UploadedPath endswith ".war" or UploadedPath endswith ".jsp"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, UploadedPath, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Cisco vManage AnyConnect Upload Handler Path Traversal (CVE-2026-20262)
id: 6f4a8e21-1c2d-4a9f-9b21-3e8c5d7f1234
description: Detects exploitation of CVE-2026-20262 via path traversal in the SdraAnyConnectFileUploadHandler — arbitrary file write into the Wildfly deployments directory.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/cisco-releases-security-updates-for.html
  - https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-sdwan-arbfw-c2rZvQ
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/16
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1505.003
logsource:
  product: cisco_sdwan
  service: vmanage_server
detection:
  selection:
    Message|contains|all:
      - 'SdraAnyConnectFileUploadHandler'
      - 'uploaded Remote Access Anyconnect profile file'
      - '../'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - None known — legitimate AnyConnect profile uploads do not traverse path.
level: high
source:cisco.sdwan "SdraAnyConnectFileUploadHandler" "uploaded Remote Access Anyconnect profile file" "../"
APPLICATION
search index=cisco_sdwan source="/var/log/nms/vmanage-server.log" "SdraAnyConnectFileUploadHandler" "uploaded Remote Access Anyconnect profile file"
| rex field=_raw "file:\s+(?<uploaded_path>\S+)\s+to\s+vManage"
| where like(uploaded_path, "%../%") OR like(uploaded_path, "%.war") OR like(uploaded_path, "%.jsp")
| stats min(_time) as first_seen, count, values(uploaded_path) as paths by host
| where first_seen >= relative_time(now(), "-7d@d")
Wildfly WFLYSRV0010 deploys non-baseline WAR on vManage AIInstallation High
Detects Wildfly auto-deploying a WAR file whose name is not part of the vManage baseline package set. The CVE-2026-20262 exploit drops a WAR into /var/lib/wildfly/standalone/deployments/ which Wildfly then auto-loads — surfacing as a WFLYSRV0010 'Deployed' record in vmanage-appserver.log for an unknown WAR name. Rationale: Pinned to the exact Wildfly log signature from the article: 'WFLYSRV0010: Deployed "suspicious.war" (runtime-name : "suspicious.war")'. Baseline allow-list derived from the standard vManage package set documented in Cisco's SD-WAN admin guide. Any WAR outside that list deployed at runtime is suspicious. Cross-checked Cisco PSIRT advisory which lists the same appserver log as the IOC source. Cross-checked against: • https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-sdwan-arbfw-c2rZvQ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/cisco-fixes-sd-wan-vmanage-flaw-exploited-in-zero-day-attacks/
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Cisco-released SD-WAN version upgrade introducing a new bundled WAR (e.g. a new statistics or analytics module) — coincides with a Cisco package install record
  • Cisco TAC engineer staging a diagnostic WAR for troubleshooting
  • Customer-developed add-on WAR deployed via a vendor-supported customisation channel (rare, enterprise-only)
  • Mid-upgrade transient state where the same baseline WAR is redeployed under a hot-patch suffix (e.g. vmanage-20.15.4.5.war)
Suppression filter
and not (WarName startswith "sdwan-" and WarName endswith "-hotpatch.war")
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the WAR filename, deployment timestamp, and the runtime-name from the WFLYSRV0010 line. SSH (or vshell) to the vManage and hash /var/lib/wildfly/standalone/deployments/<war>; pull the .deployed marker file. 2) Contain: undeploy the WAR via 'rm -f /var/lib/wildfly/standalone/deployments/<war>.deployed' to trigger Wildfly undeploy, snapshot the appliance, rotate credentials for the user whose session uploaded it (correlate via vmanage-server.log SdraAnyConnectFileUploadHandler line in the same session-id). 3) Hunt: enumerate ALL deployed WARs across the entire vManage cluster, search serviceproxy-access.log for any POST traffic to the suspicious WAR's context root, sweep edge routers for unauthorized policy/template pushes originating from this vManage in the post-deploy window.
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where SyslogMessage has "WFLYSRV0010" and SyslogMessage has "Deployed"
| extend WarName = extract(@"WFLYSRV0010:\s+Deployed\s+.(\S+?\.war)", 1, SyslogMessage)
| where isnotempty(WarName)
| where not(WarName matches regex @"^(vmanage|configuration|olap|scheduler|statistics|sdwan).*\.war$")
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), Count = count(), WarFiles = make_set(WarName) by Computer
| order by FirstSeen desc
title: Wildfly Deploys Non-Baseline WAR on Cisco vManage (CVE-2026-20262)
id: 7a5b9f32-2d3e-5ba0-ac32-4f9d6e8a2345
description: Detects Wildfly WFLYSRV0010 auto-deployment of a WAR not part of the vManage baseline package set — indicates a web-shell drop after CVE-2026-20262 file-write exploitation.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/cisco-releases-security-updates-for.html
  - https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-sdwan-arbfw-c2rZvQ
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/16
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1505.003
  - attack.t1190
logsource:
  product: cisco_sdwan
  service: vmanage_appserver
detection:
  selection:
    Message|contains: 'WFLYSRV0010: Deployed'
  filter_baseline:
    Message|contains:
      - 'vmanage.war'
      - 'configuration.war'
      - 'olap.war'
      - 'scheduler.war'
      - 'statistics-app.war'
      - 'sdwan-portal.war'
  condition: selection and not filter_baseline
falsepositives:
  - Cisco-pushed package update introducing a new WAR (rare, coincides with version bump)
level: high
source:cisco.sdwan "WFLYSRV0010: Deployed" -"vmanage.war" -"configuration.war" -"olap.war" -"scheduler.war" -"statistics-app.war" -"sdwan-portal.war"
APPLICATION
search index=cisco_sdwan source="/var/log/nms/vmanage-appserver.log" "WFLYSRV0010: Deployed"
| rex field=_raw "WFLYSRV0010:\s+Deployed\s+.(?<war_name>\S+?\.war)"
| where isnotnull(war_name) AND NOT match(war_name, "^(vmanage|configuration|olap|scheduler|statistics|sdwan).*\.war$")
| stats min(_time) as first_seen, count, values(war_name) as war_files by host
| where first_seen >= relative_time(now(), "-7d@d")
vManage service-proxy POST to attacker-deployed JSP webshell AICommand & Control High
Detects POST requests landing on a JSP path served by the vManage service-proxy that is not part of the legitimate vManage application context. After CVE-2026-20262 exploitation drops a WAR and Wildfly deploys it, the attacker interacts with index.jsp via HTTP POST through service-proxy — surfacing as a serviceproxy-access.log entry referencing the rogue context root. Rationale: Anchored on the literal access-log shape from the article: '"POST /suspicious/index.jsp HTTP/1.1" 200'. The vManage application context roots are well-known (login, app, portal, home, dataservice) and any POST to a JSP outside that set indicates an attacker-deployed web shell. Joining this UC with the WFLYSRV0010 'Deployed' UC by the same context root gives a deterministic exploit-to-interaction signal. Cross-checked against: • https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-sdwan-arbfw-c2rZvQ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/cisco-sd-wan-vmanage-vulnerability-exploit/
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1071.001
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Cisco SD-WAN upgrade introducing a new context root containing legitimate JSP endpoints (catch via version-correlated allowlist update)
  • Customer-deployed custom dashboard WAR with its own JSP (rare; would be tracked via change-management)
  • Penetration test or red-team exercise against the vManage by an authorised engagement
  • Misconfigured WAF/loadbalancer health check that probes a non-standard JSP path with a POST
Suppression filter
and not (UriPath matches regex @"^/(?:dataservice|management)/[a-z0-9_/-]+/[a-z0-9_-]+\.jsp$")
Response runbook
1) Triage: extract the JSP path, source IP, and request-id from the access log; correlate the same request-id back to vmanage-appserver.log to find which WAR served the request; pull the response status and bytes. 2) Contain: block the source IP at the edge firewall, undeploy the offending WAR (rm /var/lib/wildfly/standalone/deployments/<war>.deployed), snapshot the appliance, rotate vManage admin and netadmin credentials, force re-onboarding of any edge router whose template was modified in the same window. 3) Hunt: pivot on source IP across all vManage cluster nodes, search for outbound connections initiated by the wildfly java process to non-management IPs (vmanage normally only talks to controllers/validators), review NMS audit log for any template/policy push by the compromised session.
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where SyslogMessage has "POST" and SyslogMessage has ".jsp"
| extend UriPath = extract(@"POST\s+(/\S+\.jsp)\s+HTTP", 1, SyslogMessage)
| where isnotempty(UriPath)
| where not(UriPath matches regex @"^/(login|app|portal|home|static|dataservice)/")
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), Count = count(), JspPaths = make_set(UriPath) by Computer
| order by FirstSeen desc
title: Cisco vManage Service-Proxy POST to JSP Web Shell (CVE-2026-20262)
id: 8b6caf43-3e4f-6cb1-bd43-509e7f9b3456
description: Detects HTTP POST requests to JSP paths on the vManage service-proxy that are not part of the legitimate application context — indicates web-shell interaction following CVE-2026-20262 exploitation.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/cisco-releases-security-updates-for.html
  - https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-sdwan-arbfw-c2rZvQ
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/16
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1505.003
  - attack.t1071.001
logsource:
  product: cisco_sdwan
  service: serviceproxy_access
detection:
  selection:
    cs-method: 'POST'
    cs-uri-stem|endswith: '.jsp'
  filter_legit:
    cs-uri-stem|startswith:
      - '/login/'
      - '/app/'
      - '/portal/'
      - '/home/'
      - '/dataservice/'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
  - Cisco-internal diagnostic JSP under a new context root (rare, ties to version upgrade)
level: high
source:cisco.sdwan @http.method:POST @http.url:*.jsp -@http.url:(/login/* OR /app/* OR /portal/* OR /home/* OR /dataservice/*)
APPLICATION
search index=cisco_sdwan source="/var/log/nms/containers/service-proxy/serviceproxy-access.log" "POST" ".jsp"
| rex field=_raw "POST\s+(?<uri_path>/\S+\.jsp)\s+HTTP"
| where isnotnull(uri_path) AND NOT match(uri_path, "^/(login|app|portal|home|static|dataservice)/")
| stats min(_time) as first_seen, count, dc(src) as unique_sources, values(uri_path) as jsp_paths by host
| where first_seen >= relative_time(now(), "-7d@d")
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

CVE-2026-54420 LiteSpeed cPanel exploit: generateEcCert chained to packageUserSize for same user AIExploitation High
Detects the specific exploitation pattern for CVE-2026-54420 where an attacker with FTP/web shell access on a CloudLinux/CageFS shared host invokes the cPanel JSON API function `generateEcCert` immediately followed by `packageUserSize` for the same cPanel user within seconds. LiteSpeed explicitly states legitimate UI flows never chain these two calls — this is the highest-fidelity signature published by the vendor. Rationale: Anchored on the EXACT IOC strings published by LiteSpeed in the article body (`cpanel_jsonapi_func=generateEcCert`, `cpanel_jsonapi_func=packageUserSize`, `cert_action_entry.*geneccert`) and the vendor's explicit statement that legitimate UI flows never chain these two calls for the same user. The 10-second correlation window is generous; LiteSpeed says the calls are 'immediately' chained, so most true positives will be sub-second. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-54420
ATT&CKT1068 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Hosting provider's own automation tool (e.g. WHM bulk-provisioning script) that legitimately issues both API calls for the same user during account setup
  • Custom reseller tooling that wraps cPanel API for SSL cert provisioning and disk-quota reporting in one workflow
  • Load-testing or QA suite hammering both API endpoints
  • Migration utility (e.g. transfer_tool) that batches per-user operations
  • cPanel auto-renewal cron job if it has been customised to also report user disk usage in the same flow
Suppression filter
| where User !in~ ("root", "cpanel", "nobody") and User !startswith "_" // exclude system-context calls
| where SrcIp !in ("127.0.0.1", "::1") // exclude localhost (WHM UI proxies through loopback in some configs)
Response runbook
1) Triage: Pull the offending log lines via the LiteSpeed grep command on the affected server and confirm the chain is for ONE cPanel user (legitimate concurrent admin work would span many). Check `whoami`/`id` history and recent root-owned file creations under /home/<user>. 2) Contain: Immediately upgrade the LiteSpeed WHM Plugin to v5.3.2.1+ (bundles cPanel plugin v2.4.8). If patching is blocked, suspend the implicated cPanel user account and any FTP credentials. Snapshot the box for forensics before remediation. 3) Hunt: Search for new root-owned binaries, modified /etc/passwd or /etc/sudoers, new SSH keys in /root/.ssh, and outbound C2 from the host since the first observation. Pivot on SrcIp across other tenants of the shared host.
// Defender XDR does not natively ingest cPanel access logs. This query targets MDE-for-Linux hosts where cPanel logs are forwarded into /var/log via rsyslog and surfaced through DeviceEvents AdditionalFields, OR detects an admin running the LiteSpeed verification grep on a potentially-compromised server.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where DeviceName has_any ("cpanel","whm","cloudlinux") or FolderPath has "/usr/local/cpanel/"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_all ("grep","cpanel_jsonapi_func") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("generateEcCert","packageUserSize","geneccert")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
let Lookback = 1d;
let WindowSec = 10;
let GenCalls = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where SyslogMessage has "cpanel_jsonapi_func=generateEcCert"
    | extend User = coalesce(extract(@"cpanel_jsonapi_user=([^&\s]+)", 1, SyslogMessage), extract(@"cpanel_jsonuser=([^&\s]+)", 1, SyslogMessage), extract(@"\suser=([^&\s]+)", 1, SyslogMessage))
    | extend SrcIp = extract(@"((?:\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3})", 1, SyslogMessage)
    | project GenTime = TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, User, SrcIp, GenMsg = SyslogMessage;
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where SyslogMessage has "cpanel_jsonapi_func=packageUserSize"
| extend User = coalesce(extract(@"cpanel_jsonapi_user=([^&\s]+)", 1, SyslogMessage), extract(@"cpanel_jsonuser=([^&\s]+)", 1, SyslogMessage), extract(@"\suser=([^&\s]+)", 1, SyslogMessage))
| join kind=inner GenCalls on Computer, User
| where TimeGenerated between (GenTime .. GenTime + WindowSec * 1s)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', TimeGenerated, GenTime)
| project FirstCall_generateEcCert = GenTime, SecondCall_packageUserSize = TimeGenerated, DelaySec, Computer, User, SrcIp, GenMsg, PackageMsg = SyslogMessage
| order by FirstCall_generateEcCert desc

CVE-2026-54420 LiteSpeed cPanel exploit: burst of 7-10 concurrent generateEcCert / packageUserSize calls AIExploitation High
Detects the second IOC LiteSpeed published for CVE-2026-54420 exploitation: 7-10 concurrent calls to the vulnerable cPanel JSON API functions per exploitation attempt. The legitimate UI invokes these one at a time, so a sudden burst from a single source IP or for a single cPanel user is the exploit's race-condition trigger. Rationale: Anchored on LiteSpeed's second published IOC in the article: '7-10 concurrent calls per attempt (legitimate UI does one at a time)'. The 5-second bucket plus the 7-20 lower/upper bound directly encodes the vendor's stated exploit signature — tight enough to avoid normal cPanel UI flows, wide enough to catch attempts that issue slightly more or fewer parallel calls. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-54420
ATT&CKT1068 T1499.004
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Bulk SSL certificate renewal job (e.g. Let's Encrypt sweep across many cPanel users) hitting the same WHM server in parallel
  • Reseller migration tool issuing parallel API calls during a tenant transfer
  • Load test or synthetic monitoring against the WHM API
  • cPanel high-availability replication tooling that fans out per-user calls
  • Pen-test or vulnerability-scanner sweep replaying the published PoC against the box
Suppression filter
| where User != "" and User !in~ ("root", "cpanel", "nobody", "system") // exclude background system jobs
| where DistinctApis >= 1 // at least one of the two functions was hit
| where SrcIp != "127.0.0.1" // exclude localhost (WHM UI loopback)
Response runbook
1) Triage: Confirm whether the concurrent calls are for ONE cPanel user (exploit) or many users (likely bulk-renewal cron). Cross-reference SrcIp with known WHM admin IPs; check for the same SrcIp also hitting `generateEcCert` followed by `packageUserSize` (UC #1) for a higher-fidelity confirm. 2) Contain: Upgrade LiteSpeed WHM Plugin to v5.3.2.1+ immediately (CISA deadline is 2026-06-18). If unable to patch, block the offending SrcIp at the perimeter and suspend the implicated cPanel user pending review. 3) Hunt: Look for root-owned artefacts created in user home directories post-burst, new SUID binaries, modifications to /etc/cron.d/, and unexpected symlinks under /home/*/public_html pointing outside CageFS. Sweep all cPanel users for FTP credentials that may have been used as the initial foothold.
// Defender XDR does not ingest cPanel access logs. This query hunts MDE-for-Linux hosts where cPanel JSON API calls leak into DeviceEvents AdditionalFields via syslog forwarding, or detects the LiteSpeed verification grep being executed.
DeviceEvents

| where AdditionalFields has_any ("generateEcCert", "packageUserSize", "cert_action_entry")
| extend ApiFunc = case(AdditionalFields has "generateEcCert", "generateEcCert", AdditionalFields has "packageUserSize", "packageUserSize", "cert_action_entry_geneccert")
| summarize ConcurrentCalls = count(), DistinctApis = dcount(ApiFunc), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, AccountName, bin(Timestamp, 5s)
| where ConcurrentCalls >= 7
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog

| where SyslogMessage has_any ("cpanel_jsonapi_func=generateEcCert", "cpanel_jsonapi_func=packageUserSize") or (SyslogMessage has "cert_action_entry" and SyslogMessage has "geneccert")
| extend User = coalesce(extract(@"cpanel_jsonapi_user=([^&\s]+)", 1, SyslogMessage), extract(@"cpanel_jsonuser=([^&\s]+)", 1, SyslogMessage))
| extend SrcIp = extract(@"((?:\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3})", 1, SyslogMessage)
| extend ApiFunc = case(SyslogMessage has "generateEcCert", "generateEcCert", SyslogMessage has "packageUserSize", "packageUserSize", "cert_action_entry_geneccert")
| summarize ConcurrentCalls = count(), DistinctApis = dcount(ApiFunc), CallTypes = make_set(ApiFunc), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by Computer, User, SrcIp, bin_time = bin(TimeGenerated, 5s)

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-54420")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain

status: experimental
description: |

references:

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:

            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'

falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match
level: critical
